about.title: ohmail — demo
about.p1: A demo mailbox, invented for it — nobody real, nothing real. Every key and every click works, and none of it leaves this tab: there is no network here at all.
about.p2: The Screener holds first-time senders until you decide. One click files a sender to Ohbox, Reads or Receipts — the ✓ half also marks the held mail read — and the decision becomes a rule for future mail. Reads and Receipts share a skim stream where scrolling past an item marks it seen at the waterline. Tags group messages across views without moving them.

ai.title: AI proposes. You decide.
ai.body: Rules run first and do the bulk of the work with no AI at all — the design goal is that most of your mail is filed deterministically, by rules you can read and change. Where judgment actually helps, ohmail offers something: a door for a new sender, a draft in your voice, a nudge for a thread that went quiet. Every one of them waits for your yes, and nothing ever sends itself.
ai.status: The AI features are built and tested against the model port, but no live model is connected in production yet — the managed AI actions switch on with the beta, and the metering and spend limits that govern them are already in place.
ai.toggleBody: This is the same mail, twice. Flip the switch — nothing breaks, nothing goes missing. That is the point: ohmail is a complete mail client with the AI switched off, and a faster one with it on.
ai.captionOn: Suggestions and drafts — proposed, never performed.
ai.captionOff: Rules only. Same mail, same folders, nothing missing.
ai.rowNewOnLine: Suggested from how you handled her studio before. Press ↵ to accept.

ai.rowReplyDraft: Ciao Giulia, perfetto — il 4 agosto va benissimo. La consegna resta all’atelier, come sempre. Grazie mille!
ai.rowReplyOnLine: Sits in the composer as a proposal. You send it, or you rewrite it, or you delete it.
ai.rowReplyOffLine: Reply — a blank composer, exactly like every other mail app.
ai.rowCodeLine: Never sent to AI — in either state. Structural, not a setting.
ai.rowRuleLine: Filed by rule: list header, known newsletter. No AI in either state.
ai.pointGrad: Decide the same way three times and ohmail asks to make it a rule. You approve it once — from then on it runs deterministically, with no AI at all.
ai.pointOtp: When mail carries a verification code or login link, it is never sent to AI, never forwarded, and stored redacted — structurally, with no setting to turn it off.
ai.pointByoTitle: Your key, your machine — or ours
ai.pointByo: The plan for Desktop: bring your own API key, or run a local model so nothing leaves your machine — that arrives with the local engine, and is not built yet. On Cloud: a monthly bag of AI actions is included, and mail keeps flowing rules-only when it runs out.

fast.body: Every mailbox is mirrored locally, so search answers as you type — typo-tolerant, scoped, and just as quick with the wifi off. Tags instead of folder gymnastics. Native apps that open before you finish the thought.
fast.pointC: Native on desktop, instant mirror everywhere
fast.q1Note: Typos are fine — fuzzy matching, on your own machine.
fast.q2Note: Scope it: from, tag, mailbox, before, has.
fast.q3Note: One tag, every mailbox — no folder gymnastics.

pricing.title: Desktop is free. The cloud is optional.
pricing.sub: ohmail Desktop will be the full product — free, standalone, no account, no artificial limits. Cloud is for when you want your mail on your phone, on the web, and working while you sleep. An AI action is one piece of AI work — a Screener suggestion, a summary, a draft — and if you ever run out, mail keeps flowing rules-only. Never a surprise charge. Cloud is open today, trial first and no card. Desktop is a free download today, and what you download is the interface: the local mail engine is what we are building now.
pricing.desktopStatusNote: Today the Desktop apps are a preview of the interface, running on a small fictional mailbox. They contain no IMAP client and make no network connections at all. The local mail engine is what we are building now.

compare.title: Your mailbox, or theirs.
compare.sub: We like the apps that rethink mail — the ones that screen senders, the ones that add AI to your inbox. They pushed the craft forward and we admire the work. What we don't like is where the organization ends up: inside someone else's app, staying behind when you go. So this table is about one axis only — whose mailbox it is.
compare.addressesUs: Stays exactly where it is — ohmail connects over IMAP
compare.addressesHey: Mail moves to HEY. Your address can come along (HEY for Domains); your existing mailbox can't.
compare.addressesOverlays: Stays put — but only Gmail and Outlook qualify
compare.foldersUs: Real IMAP folders on your server, readable by any client
compare.foldersHey: In HEY's apps only — no IMAP or POP access
compare.foldersOverlays: In their apps and cloud, via provider APIs
compare.leaveHey: Mail exports as one MBOX file; the organization stays behind
compare.leaveOverlays: Some of it syncs back as labels; the rest stays behind
compare.offlineUs: Desktop is designed to run fully on your machine — in development, not shipped
compare.offlineHey: Native apps, but the service is cloud-only
compare.offlineOverlays: Native apps; processing in their cloud
compare.aiUs: Optional and gated — every suggestion waits for your yes
compare.aiOverlays: Built in, runs in their cloud
compare.note: Compared as of July 2026, from each product's own published documentation. The Superhuman column is being re-checked following Grammarly's acquisition.
compare.usLine: ohmail's answer to every row is the same answer: it's your mailbox. Several of them, in fact — ohmail organizes five, ten, fifty IMAP mailboxes at once, drafts replies in your voice, learns your decisions into rules you can read and change, and never asks you to change your address, your provider, or your other mail apps.
compare.goodwill: These are good products made by people who care about mail. The right model is the one that fits your life, and it may not be ours — that is a fine outcome. We only insist on one thing: the choice should stay yours, and so should the mailbox.

data.title: Where your mail lives.
data.sub: The honest answer is different per tier — so here it is, per tier.
data.desktopBody: Desktop is designed so your mail never touches our servers: sync, rules and search all run on your machine. That design is not shipped yet — today's Desktop apps are a preview of the interface with no mailbox connection at all, and the local engine is in development.
data.desktopNote: Desktop-only is meant to be a complete way to use ohmail, forever — no account, no cloud, nothing of yours on our side, and not a trial version of anything. We will say here the day the engine lands.
data.cloudBody: Cloud keeps a full copy of your mail — bodies, headers, subjects and senders, not just metadata — on EU servers, for one purpose: delivering sync, push and search to your devices. Storage is encrypted at rest, connections between your devices and ohmail are encrypted in transit, and your mailbox credentials are additionally encrypted at the application level. It is not end-to-end encrypted — the service has to read mail to file and search it, and a small number of people with production database access could technically read it. Never sold, never mined, never used for anything but serving you. Deleting your account erases that data from live systems immediately and from backups within 30 days. The full privacy policy, naming exactly who can access what, publishes before the first real mailbox connects; the subprocessor and retention list linked in the footer is live today.
data.cloudNote: Why a cloud exists at all: your phone can’t keep a connection to your mailbox open all day — the battery and the operating system won’t allow it. Something has to stay awake to notice new mail and tap you on the shoulder. That is what Cloud is for — push, mobile and the web — and doing that job is why it holds a copy of your mail rather than only your rules.
data.aiBody: AI requests go to Anthropic under commercial API terms: your mail is never used to train models, and Anthropic retains requests only briefly under its standard policy (currently up to 30 days). We have not yet negotiated a zero-retention agreement, and we will say so here when we do. Sensitive mail — verification codes, logins — is never sent to AI at all. That's structural, not a setting. No live model is connected in production yet; the managed AI actions switch on with the beta.

providers.title: If it speaks IMAP, ohmail organizes it.
providers.any: …and any IMAP mailbox, including your own server.
providers.note: Microsoft 365 and Outlook.com connect the way every other mailbox does: over IMAP. Native Exchange sync — Microsoft Graph, and signing in with Microsoft instead of an app password — is on the roadmap and not shipped yet; we’ll say so here the day it is.

faq.title: Questions, answered.
faq.q1: What happens to my existing folders?
faq.a1: Nothing destructive. The folders you already have are left exactly as they are; ohmail organizes new mail into real IMAP folders on your server. Everything stays visible to any other mail client, on any device.
faq.a2: Anytime. Your mail never needs exporting — the originals live on your own server, in ordinary folders ohmail created in place, and nothing we do touches them. Be clear about what Cloud holds, though: a full copy of that mail — bodies, headers, subjects and senders — alongside your rules, tags and notes, because that is what makes search and push work. All of it is deleted with your account.
faq.a3: On Cloud: on our servers, within your included actions — that is the part being wired for the beta, and no live model is connected in production yet. On Desktop the plan is that you point it wherever you like — your own API key, or a local model so nothing leaves your machine — and that arrives with the local engine rather than today. Either way, rules with no AI at all run first and are meant to handle most mail — and you can switch the AI off entirely without losing a single feature that files your mail.
faq.q4: What exactly is an AI action?
faq.a4: One unit of AI work: a Screener suggestion for a new sender, a summary, a drafted reply. When your monthly actions run out, mail keeps flowing rules-only until the next cycle. There are no overage charges — ever.
faq.a5: Not as a matter of practice, and our admin tools do not display message content — every response the console can produce is checked by a test that writes a marker into every text column of every table and fails if any of it reaches a staff response. The database itself does not yet refuse those columns to staff tooling: the column-restricted role that would enforce this below the application is built and tested but not yet live, and we will not claim it until it is. The honest fine print: Cloud mail is stored unencrypted at the application level and is not end-to-end encrypted, so someone with production database access could technically read it; that access is held by very few people, and the product privacy policy will spell out who and under what conditions when it publishes, before the first real mailbox connects. On Desktop the question won't arise — your mail is never meant to reach our servers — but the local engine is still in development. The spy-pixel blocker is built and tested, and is not yet switched on in the reading path; it blocks trackers and records who tried once it is.
faq.a6: Any IMAP mailbox: your own domain at Metanet or Infomaniak, iCloud, Gmail, Outlook, a self-hosted server. If it speaks IMAP, ohmail organizes it in place. Native Exchange sync over Microsoft Graph is on the roadmap; today Microsoft 365 connects over IMAP like everything else.
faq.q7: Is there a trial for Cloud?
faq.a7: Yes — 14 days, no card. It is the whole product except the managed AI actions: rules, sync, push, mobile and web all run, and the included AI actions begin when a subscription does. Desktop needs no trial at all; it is simply free.
faq.q8: Desktop or Cloud — what’s the real difference?
faq.a8: The same model, the same vocabulary, and deliberately not the same privacy posture — that is the honest difference. Desktop is free and is being built to be fully standalone: all processing local, no account, no artificial limits, with your own AI key or a local model. It is not there yet; today it is a preview of the interface with no mailbox connection. Cloud adds the web and mobile apps, push notifications, always-on processing while your computer sleeps, and AI included from $9 a month — and it holds a copy of your mail on our servers to do that. Cloud is open today; the desktop apps are downloadable now as an interface preview.

account.title: Delete your account
account.lead: Signed in as {email}. This cannot be undone.
account.signOutBody: Ends this session and removes the mail cached in this browser. Your mailbox and your account are untouched.
account.mail: Your mail is on your own server, in the ohmail folders it is filed into. This deletes our copy; your mailbox stays exactly as organized as it is now.
account.gone2: Every mailbox you connected, and the stored credentials for it.
account.gone3: Every message, thread, contact and note we mirrored, with your rules, screener decisions and workflows.
account.gone4: Your passkeys, authenticator and recovery codes, and every session on every device.
account.goneWhen: One database transaction, immediately, and the copy in this browser is wiped too.
account.kept1: One billing row with a random id and no name, plus the credit ledger, the subscription record and the link to Stripe. Your address on it is overwritten. Financial records carry a retention obligation that Art. 17(3)(b) preserves.
account.keptSub: Your {plan} subscription is cancelled immediately as part of this. The days already paid for are not refunded.
account.backups: Backups expire on their own schedule.
account.confirmBody: This is the most destructive thing the product can do, so a signed-in browser is not enough for it: your password and your second factor, again, now.
account.factorBody: The next successful factor erases the account for {email}. There is no further step after it.
account.mismatch: Those credentials belong to a different account, so nothing was deleted. Sign in as the account you want to delete and try again.
account.doneBody: It is gone from our live systems and you are signed out on every device. Your mailbox is untouched — open it in any mail app and the ohmail folders are still there.
account.doneSubFailed: We could not reach Stripe to cancel your subscription. Your account is erased, but the subscription may still be active — write to support@ohmail.app and we will cancel it.

account.signedOutBody: Deleting an account needs a live session on that account.
account.unavailableBody: This copy of ohmail has no server attached, so there is no account to delete.
